facts.claim: Bedside sites (Goo) are cleaned only by a per-site countdown: every cleaningDay days the site is set completely clean and the counter is reset. With cleaningDay=1.0 in every study, all 30 sites are cleaned once a day. Because all sites are created together at init and step every tick, they share one phase: cleaning happens at total_ticks % 2592 == 0, after all workers have stepped in that tick (scheduler insertion order is workers, then Bed/Patient/Goo per bed).

facts.claim: No site is cleaned at patient discharge, admission or isolation relocation, and there is no natural decay. Goo.handwash has exactly one caller (Goo.step). The only other `colonized = False` writes are HCW hand clears and role resets. The holdout data agree: every arm of all 1,536 records has exactly 1680 scheduled clears (30 sites x 56 days), zero contaminated sites at both daily boundaries, and depositions equal to dirty scheduled clears in every profile and arm.
facts.evidence: grep: agents.py:547 is the only `self.handwash()` call inside Goo; other `colonized = False` writes are at agents.py:282, 297, 368, 392, 402, all on HCWs. CPEmodel.py:301-307 `_remove_discharged` only does grid.remove_agent/schedule.remove; CPEmodel.py:278-286 `admit_patient` only places a Patient; agents.py:494-502 Bed.step only admits; CPEmodel.py:309-312 `_move_patient` only does grid.move_agent + checkIsolated. Goo.step (agents.py:542-548) has no decay term. instrumented_model.py:106-115 counts every Goo.handwash as scheduled_clear. Data: route_opportunity_table.md (scheduled_clear=860160=512x1680 per profile/arm; e.g. Independent control has 44878 dirty clears and 44878 depositions).

facts.claim: _relocate_detected_patients runs after every tick when isolate_sick=True (it is True in all studies). For each shared bed in list order holding a detected (`positive`) patient, the carrier goes to the FIRST isolation bed in isol_beds order whose filledSick is False, whether that bed is empty or occupied. An empty isolation bed later in the list is not preferred. If the chosen bed is occupied, its occupant is moved into the carrier's vacated shared bed. If every isolation bed holds a detected carrier, the carrier stays in the shared bed.
facts.evidence: CPEmodel.py:345-349 `self._remove_discharged(); self.refresh_beds(); if self.isolate_sick: self._relocate_detected_patients()`; CPEmodel.py:314-332 `for isolated_bed in self.isol_beds: isolated_bed.checkFilled(); if isolated_bed.filledSick: continue; other = next((a for a in ... if a.isPatient), None); self._move_patient(sick, isolated_bed.pos); if other is not None: self._move_patient(other, bed.pos) ... break`; run.py:33 `isolate_sick=True`.

facts.claim: The patient displaced into the carrier's shared bed is either a noncarrier (susceptible) or an imported carrier that no worker has contacted yet. filledSick is True only for a detected (`positive`) occupant. `positive` is set only by testCRE during an HCW contact with a colonized patient and is never cleared. Acquired carriers are tested in the same contact in which they acquire.
facts.evidence: agents.py:504-514 checkFilled: `if self.filled and cellmate.positive: self.filledSick = True`; agents.py:169-174 testCRE sets `other.positive = True` (test_rate = true_positive_rate = 1 at :68-69); agents.py:220-222 `if other.isPatient and other.colonized: self.testCRE(other)`, run after the transmission draw; agents.py:434 `self.positive = False` at admission; no other write to positive.

facts.claim: Bedside sites and care zones belong to fixed bed positions, not to patients. Goo agents never move. A patient moved into a bed therefore takes over that bed's site, which may be contaminated, and it is not cleaned until the next daily clear. Isolation beds have their own sites (all 30 beds have one). 16 of the 30 beds are isolation beds and 14 are shared. Neither the manuscript nor the supplement states this count.
facts.evidence: CPEmodel.py:170-172 comment `Zones belong to fixed bed locations, never patient IDs`; CPEmodel.py:221-230 `isolated = x in {1, 3, 5, 7, 23, 25, 27, 29}` ... `environment_position = (x, y-1 if y > 5 else y+1)`; `care_zone_by_position[(x, y)] = bed.unique_id`; `self._place(Goo(-30-i, ...))`. Instantiating the model (no bytecode written) gave isol_beds=16, shared_beds=14, and 16 of 30 Goo with isolated=True. grep of manuscript.tex and supplement.tex found no isolation-bed count.

facts.claim: The 0.6 isolation multiplier applies to sites as well as patients. HCW.spread multiplies by isolation_factor whenever the contacted object's `isolated` flag is True. Goo sets that flag from x-position, the same rule Patient uses, so contacts with isolation-bed sites are scaled in both directions (deposition and pickup). Bed and IsolatedBed play no part.

facts.claim: The Bed and IsolatedBed docstrings are wrong. Bed agents are never transmission surfaces: spread only considers patients and Goo, Bed.colonized is always False and never read or written, and nothing cleans after a patient leaves. A Bed only admits patients and reports occupancy, and isBed is used only to count bed visits. IsolatedBed adds nothing beyond the isIsolatedBed flag; the isolation effect comes from position-based flags on Patient and Goo. The Patient docstring 'Cannot move' is also wrong, given the relocation swap.

facts.claim: Route labels and opportunity counts. When a patient acquires, the label comes from the acquiring worker's `_response_origin`: the successful pickup that began its current uncleared hand-contamination episode. A pickup is registered only when the worker's hands are clean, and the origin is cleared by an effective hand clear or a role reset. The labels are patient_pickup, own_zone_environment_pickup, other_zone_environment_pickup, own_zone_environment_pickup_after_readmission and untracked_hand; untracked_hand is asserted to be 0. The opportunity key is str(n) or 'unknown', where n is the worker's hygiene_opportunity_count at transfer minus the count at pickup. That counter increases on every HCW.handwash() call, which under zone_separate means every care-zone entry and exit. So n is the number of hygiene opportunities the contamination survived between pickup and transfer, counting missed actions and, when e<1, completed but ineffective ones. Role resets are not opportunities. The three histograms are filled together and each sums to acquired_colonizations.
facts.evidence: instrumented_model.py:82-85 `elif not self.colonized and other.colonized: ... self.model._observe_pickup(self, other)`; :151 `'opportunities_at_pickup': worker.hygiene_opportunity_count`; :171-192 `_observe_acquisition`: `n = worker.hygiene_opportunity_count - origin['opportunities_at_pickup']`, route branches, `gap = 'unknown' if n is None else str(n)`, `acquisitions_by_route_and_opportunities[route + '|' + gap] += 1`; :91-104 handwash wrapper clears origin on clean hands; :194-199 implicit-reset clearing; :210-213 sum and untracked asserts; agents.py:260 `self._count_hygiene('hygiene_opportunity_count')` at the top of handwash; agents.py:237-249 zone entry/exit handwash calls.

facts.claim: The '_after_readmission' label requires the site's contamination lineage to predate the latest admission to that bed AND the acquiring patient to be that latest admission. A relocation swap is not an admission, so contamination a swapped-in patient inherits from the carrier's site is labelled plain own_zone_environment_pickup. The histograms cannot separate it from contamination deposited during the current stay. Under zone_separate, any change of zone costs an exit and an entry opportunity, so 0 opportunities means pickup and transfer within one zone visit. In the data every 0-opportunity acquisition follows a site pickup, and patient_pickup|0 and other_zone|0 are 0 in all arms. Because pickups register only on clean hands, if the entry wash fails on already dirty hands the same visit is labelled with the earlier origin and n>=2.

d1_summary:
Sources: 1,536 holdout records (448 cluster + 64 local seeds for each of 3 profiles), 3,072 arm-records. I used arms.<arm>.observation.response_counts, which the runner already stores as final_snapshot minus warmup_snapshot. I re-derived that difference for every record and it matched exactly. For each record and arm, the joint route|opportunity histogram summed to observation.acquired_colonizations, and untracked_hand was 0.

Pooled site/total counts reproduce S13 exactly: 1717/2375 and 627/770; 894/2255 and 405/995; 885/2352 and 671/1718.

Site pickup with 0 opportunities, as a share of all acquisitions (control vs policy):
- Independent: 57.8% vs 71.0%
- Clustered misses: 25.0% vs 27.6%
- Imperfect clearing: 23.6% vs 25.6%
- As a share of site-labelled acquisitions: 80.0/87.2, 63.0/67.9 and 62.6/65.6%.

Own-zone, earlier-admission (carry-over) labels: 450/2375 vs 319/770; 75/2255 vs 53/995; 62/2352 vs 58/1718. Almost all are at 0 opportunities.

Structural checks:
- patient_pickup|0 and other_zone|0 are 0 in every arm, and all gaps are even.
- Every arm has 1680 scheduled clears and zero dirty sites at daily boundaries.
- Depositions equal dirty clears.

Caveats:
- These are passive proximate labels, not causal shares.
- Under policy, the larger share of 0-opportunity site pickups partly reflects the fact that a pickup is registered only on clean hands.
- Relocation-inherited site contamination is labelled plain own-zone.
